name: Mary Silva
bio: Mary Silva is a clinical audiologist with about 20 years of practice, including seven as a managing partner, and holds a Doctor of Audiology from Salus University. She has served as a Republican precinct committee officer in Snohomish and King counties and also ran for this seat in 2024. She is the Republican nominee for Washington's 1st Congressional District.

platform.point: Bring semiconductor manufacturing home, reform H-1B visas to favor American workers and expand apprenticeships.
Tighten border and clearance security and investigate foreign penetration of critical infrastructure.
Conduct a full Pentagon audit and cut intelligence contractor costs.
Require voter ID and create a midweek voting holiday.
Protect informed consent and parents' authority over children's health care.
End warrantless mass surveillance and enforce Fourth Amendment limits on data collection.
Address offshore tax havens and corporate tax avoidance, and use policy incentives to bring manufacturing jobs back.
Lower regulatory barriers and widen access to capital for local small and mid-sized businesses.

economy.evidence: Her voters' guide statement backs incentives for domestic production and action on offshore tax havens, alongside lower regulatory barriers for small firms.

security.evidence: Calls for ending warrantless mass surveillance such as license-plate camera networks and requiring warrants for location and communications data.

immigration.evidence: Wants stronger border security and H-1B reform prioritizing American workers.

foreign.evidence: General statement: her site favors peaceful means over military intervention and a full Pentagon audit, and features a video critical of Israel's prime minister.

tech.evidence: Proposes federal privacy standards requiring warrants before agencies or third-party vendors collect or share location data, and a ban on foreign-linked police technology.

notes: Searched her campaign site (home and issues pages), the Washington Secretary of State voters' guide and Wikipedia race pages. No public positions were found on welfare programs, abortion, guns, energy, schools or religion.

name: Chris D. Chung
bio: Chris D. Chung is a pharmacist who has owned a pharmacy in the Tacoma-Lakewood area for 33 years and is a graduate of St. John's University College of Pharmacy. He ran in the 2024 primary for Washington insurance commissioner as a Democrat and in the 2025 Federal Way mayoral primary. He is the Republican nominee for Washington's 10th Congressional District.

platform.point: Wants to ease the burden of rising living and housing costs on district families.
Pledges to improve access to health care and education.
Wants veterans and people who served the community treated with respect and given fuller support.

welfare.evidence: General statement: his voters' guide statement pledges to improve access to health care and education for families.

notes: Searched the Washington Secretary of State voters' guide, Wikipedia race pages and 2024 insurance commissioner coverage; no campaign website or social accounts were found. His only public statement is general, so most topics remain unknown.

name: Teresa Fox
bio: Teresa Fox is a lifelong Bremerton resident with about 30 years in regulatory compliance and workplace safety, including safety work for the Navy's inactive ships office, Washington Labor and Industries, Olympic College and an Alaska fish processing vessel. She has served five years as a Kitsap County Republican precinct committee officer. She is the Republican nominee for Washington's 6th Congressional District.

platform.point: Opposes a state income tax and the Climate Commitment Act, arguing Washingtonians are overburdened by government.
Proposes a federal public safety floor giving local agencies incentives to hire and keep police officers.
Shift defense dollars from consultants to shipyard workers and equipment, and avoid rushed electrification of support vessels.
Opposes transgender women competing in women's sports and sharing girls' locker rooms.
Use telehealth and financial incentives to bring specialists and providers to underserved rural areas.
Supports congressional term limits and has signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge.

economy.evidence: General statement: opposes a state income tax and wants businesses to operate without constant government interference.

liberty.evidence: On LGBTQ issues, opposes transgender women competing in women's sports under Title IX; no stated positions on abortion, guns, drugs or speech.

security.evidence: Proposes federal incentives for local agencies to hire and retain more police officers.

energy.evidence: Opposes the Climate Commitment Act and federal mandates for rapid electrification of shipyard support vessels.

notes: Read her campaign site's home, about and mission content and her Washington voters' guide statement; a local launch article was blocked. No positions were found on immigration, foreign policy, welfare, technology, schools or religion.

name: Doug Basler
bio: Doug Basler founded and runs Prologue Digital, an advertising and video production company, and has worked in media and marketing since 1990. He is a former vice chair of the King County Republican Party and former youth and worship pastor who attended Multnomah University. He has run for this seat in several previous elections.

platform.point: Focuses on rising housing, grocery and tax costs for families.
Wants to widen opportunity for entrepreneurship, homeownership and career advancement.
Wants compassion for people in crisis combined with accountability for crime.
Opposes the Climate Commitment Act and high gas taxes over their effect on costs.

economy.evidence: General statement: says big-government policies make it harder to build, hire and afford, and favors a business-friendly climate.

energy.evidence: Opposes Washington's Climate Commitment Act, citing higher energy costs.

notes: Checked his campaign site (home, about, media and other pages) and his Washington voters' guide statement, which matches the about page. No stated positions were found on welfare, social issues, immigration, foreign policy, technology or schools.

name: Tim Rogers
bio: Tim Rogers was born and raised in Milwaukee, graduated from North Division High School and studied at UW-Parkside and MATC. He has worked for nearly 30 years delivering gift baskets and newspapers for local businesses. He was the Republican nominee for Wisconsin's 4th District in earlier cycles and is the nominee again in 2026.

platform.point: Supports universal school choice and voucher programs, citing poor results in Milwaukee Public Schools.
Wants harsh sentences for violent crime and automatic restoration of rights once a sentence is complete.
Declare a clean water emergency and replace aging lead pipes in cities like Milwaukee.
Cut government spending, let taxpayers keep more money and end the progressive income tax system.
Proposes eliminating property taxes nationwide.

economy.evidence: Says he would work to end the progressive tax system, cut spending and eliminate property taxes.

welfare.evidence: General statement: wants less government spending and federal agencies and programs to shrink through attrition.

education.evidence: Supports universal school choice and voucher programs and argues public school spending is unconstitutional.

notes: Found his campaign site (linked from Wikipedia) and read its about, issues and blog pages; some content dates from earlier campaigns. No positions were found on social issues, policing powers, immigration, foreign policy, energy or technology.

name: Eric Barlow
bio: Eric Barlow, a Gillette-born Marine Corps veteran and large-animal veterinarian with a DVM from Colorado State University, served on the Wyoming Livestock Board before winning a Wyoming House seat in 2012. He served as House majority leader and as speaker from 2021 to 2023 and has represented Senate District 23 since 2023. He won the 2026 Republican primary for governor.

platform.point: Keep the state living within its means through cash-based budgeting and transparency.
Protect coal, oil, gas and uranium production and streamline permitting.
Keep school decisions local and give parents a strong role.
Support protections for the unborn along with maternal health resources.
Defend the Second Amendment and restore firearm rights to eligible citizens.
Make health care a day-one priority, with a strike team to find near-term steps on access and cost.
Defend private property and water rights against eminent-domain and zoning overreach.

economy.evidence: Backs cash-based budgeting and property tax relief, cosponsored a 2025 coal severance tax cut and voted against fuel tax increases.

welfare.evidence: As speaker, voted for HB0162 (2021), a bill to expand Medicaid eligibility that passed the Wyoming House 32-28.

liberty.evidence: Describes himself as firmly anti-abortion and voted for Wyoming's girls' sports and minor gender-transition treatment bans, while backing gun rights and concealed carry (abortion, LGBTQ, guns).

security.evidence: General statement: pledges training, resources and support for law enforcement while respecting local control.

immigration.evidence: Says he voted for Wyoming's 2025 sanctuary-city ban, though he opposed introducing a 2016 bill restricting public benefits.

energy.evidence: Supported legislation protecting coal, oil, gas and uranium production.

education.evidence: Voted against the universal education savings account bill HB0199 on Senate third reading in 2025, but supported the 2024 K-12 parental rights law.

notes: Read his campaign positions, health care, biography and record pages, Wyoming Legislature roll calls (HB0162 of 2021 and HB0199 of 2025) and WyoFile coverage. No stated positions were found on foreign policy, technology regulation or religion in public life.

name: Kenneth Casner
bio: Kenneth Casner, of Elk Mountain, is the Democratic nominee for Governor of Wyoming in 2026 and was unopposed in the primary. He previously ran for governor in 2002 and in the 2018 Democratic primary, where he received about 6 percent of the vote.

platform.point: Supports creating a state income tax.
Wants public school funding and more focus on teaching history.
Runs without asking for donations and says he speaks for working-class Wyomingites.

economy.evidence: Supports creating a state income tax in Wyoming, which has none.

education.evidence: Calls for public school funding and more focus on history education; a general statement.

notes: No campaign website; positions come from Wyoming Public Media and Oil City News. He did not answer the WyoFile questionnaire.

name: Steve Parsons
bio: Steve G. Parsons holds a Ph.D. in economics, is a retired consultant who advised companies on regulation, and taught the economics of technology to engineering graduate students at Washington University in St. Louis for over 20 years. He moved to Lakeview, Arkansas, in 2016. He was the Libertarian nominee for Arkansas's 1st District in 2024 and is running again in 2026.

platform.point: Reduce government intrusion in personal and business decisions.
Cut inflation through lower federal spending, fewer regulations, ending tariffs and limiting the Federal Reserve's money creation.
Reduce regulatory burdens and end corporate welfare, including repeal of the Jones Act shipping rules.
End extensive foreign aid and overseas military commitments.
Reform incarceration and the handling of substance abuse and mental health.
Eliminate tariffs and reform the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement's auto rules, which he says raise prices.
Speed up green cards and work visas, bar noncitizens from welfare and create clearer paths to permanent residency.
Cut or eliminate federal agencies including FEMA and the U.S. Department of Education.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting regulations, federal spending and corporate subsidies, and eliminating tariffs.

welfare.evidence: Wants means-tested benefits limited to citizens and proposes eliminating FEMA and farm subsidies.

liberty.evidence: Wants marijuana removed from Schedule I and fewer personal-choice rules (drugs), while saying abortion is a state matter with rape and incest exceptions (abortion).

security.evidence: Criticizes FBI surveillance of Americans as a Fourth Amendment violation and backs reducing incarceration.

immigration.evidence: Wants faster green cards and work visas and a clearer path to legal residency, alongside citizen-only welfare and deporting convicted criminals to Mexico.

foreign.evidence: Wants to end extensive foreign aid and entangling alliances, questioning NATO commitments and aid to Israel.

energy.evidence: General statement: criticizes subsidies in the Inflation Reduction Act and infrastructure law as corporate welfare.

education.evidence: General statement: says there is no constitutional basis for a federal Department of Education and wants education decisions left to states and localities.

notes: Read every page of his campaign site, including platform, debate notes, immigration, regulation, foreign policy and agency pages. No positions were found on technology regulation or religion in public life.
